content:
Yesterday we saw how Dathan and Abiram rewrote their own history.

They called Egypt a land of milk and honey, and they blamed Moses for a wilderness that their own unbelief had brought upon them. Now we must bring this lesson close to our own lives, because the spirit of these two men can quietly enter the heart of the New Creation as well. Let us think about how this happens, so that we may watch and pray and not fall into the same snare.

Perhaps there was a brother or a sister whom God once used in a very important way in our life. Maybe that person first opened the Scriptures to us. Perhaps it was through them that we began to see the false teachings we had believed for many years. They may have studied with us patiently, corrected our mistakes gently, encouraged us to come out of spiritual darkness,
and walked beside us as we began to follow the truth. And at first our hearts were full of thankfulness. We could hardly believe that God had shown us such kindness through them.

But then the wilderness begins. Following the truth does not mean that every earthly trouble suddenly disappears. Our money problems may not vanish. Our family struggles may go on. We may be misunderstood by people we love. Some may reject us because of what we now believe. Our prayers may not be answered in the way we had hoped. And we may even discover faults and weaknesses among the very brothers and sisters we now walk with.

Perhaps someone disappoints us. Perhaps we had expected more love,more attention, more recognition, or more support than we received.

And then a dangerous thought can slip into the mind. It whispers, “Ever since I came here, my life has become difficult.” And soon another thought follows, “If that brother had never brought me here, I would not be going through all this.” And at last it becomes, “It is because of you that I came here.” Do we hear it? This is the very voice of Dathan and Abiram. They looked at Moses and said, in effect, you brought us out, and now look what has happened to us. We must be very careful, for the same words can form in our own mouths without our noticing.

So let us remember something important. The brother or sister who showed us the truth never promised us an easy earthly Canaan of money, health, comfort, and a trouble-free life. Our calling in Christ is not a promise that every circumstance will quickly become pleasant. Our Master Himself told us plainly, “In the world you will have trouble.” If we secretly came into the truth hoping that God would now give us a better job, more money, perfect health, a peaceful home, or an easy road, then disappointment will one day bring that hidden hope to the surface. And when it does, we may begin to blame the messenger for promises the messenger never made.

Now we must be careful to hold two things apart, for they are not the same.

If a brother truly sins against God, his wrong can and should be dealt with in the way the Scriptures teach. We are not asked to pretend that wrongdoing did not happen, nor to excuse sin simply because someone once helped us. But we must never blame a person merely because Yahweh used them to open our eyes. Paul once asked the Galatians a piercing question, “Have I now become your enemy because I tell you the truth?” That is a question worth keeping before us. A person who once helped us can suddenly seem like our enemy,not because they have changed, but because our own heart has changed.

There is one more danger, and it is a serious one. Dathan and Abiram did not only attack Moses. They also began to speak well of Egypt. This can happen to us too. When following Christ becomes hard, the old life can begin to look attractive again. We may think, “Before I knew all this truth, life was easier. When I lived like the world or in my old Church, I had more friends. Maybe I was happier back then.” But we must be careful. We must not rename Egypt. Egypt was still Egypt. Bondage does not become freedom simply because the wilderness is difficult. The hardness of the road does not prove that our deliverance was a mistake.

In the same way, disappointment with people must never turn into rebellion against God. We must not say, “Because this brother failed me, the truth must be false,” or “Because I had a painful experience among the brethren, I should go back to my former life and former doctrines.” The truth does not become false because someone behaved badly. Christ does not become unfaithful because a Christian let us down. Yahweh does not become our enemy because the journey became difficult. The one who helped us may have pointed us to the road, but Christ alone is our Leader. That brother did not redeem us.

That sister did not buy us with her blood. They helped us to see, but our covenant is with Yahweh through Christ. So let us take responsibility for our own walk, examine our own hearts, forgive where forgiveness is needed, and keep our eyes fixed upon Christ, the author and finisher of our faith.

title: Prayer
text:
Our loving Father Yahweh, we thank You for every brother and sister You have used to lead us toward the light of Your truth. Keep us from ever turning a helper into an enemy simply because our road has become hard. Save us from the bitterness that rewrites our history and makes the darkness we left behind look sweet. Help us to hold fast to two things at once, to deal rightly with real wrongs in the way Your Word teaches, yet never to accuse the faithful without cause. When we are disappointed, let us not blame others for the fruit of our own choices, but let us search our own hearts before You. Above all, helps us to fix our eyes upon Your Son, our Master, and not upon men, for He alone redeemed us with His own blood. Keep us walking faithfully in the wilderness until we reach the rest You have promised.

In Christ name we pray. Amen.
